decision: Session start takes the per-home lock before any step that changes state, and the changing steps run only when the session holds it.
alternatives: Run bootstrap first and take the lock afterwards, as the older instructions did (the script header names the old order).
tradeoff: A session that loses the lock changes nothing and stays read-only, but it also cannot run the repairs bootstrap would have made until a later session holds the lock.
reversal_cost: Moderate (inferred): the drain and the bootstrap sweeps each test whether the session holds the lock.
authors_say: acquire the per-home session lock FIRST, before any

decision: The blocking part of session start makes no external-network call; network checks run in a deferred stage outside the digest's bound.
alternatives: Make the network checks part of the digest, as they once were (the header says each was individually unbounded).
tradeoff: The first turn starts sooner and one unreachable remote cannot truncate the digest, but the network results arrive later and the agent must treat them as unfinished until they report.
reversal_cost: Moderate (inferred): the digest, the deferred worker and the network report command all assume the split.

decision: Re-arming the watcher lives in a component above the one-shot watcher process, not in a step the model must remember.
alternatives: Have the model re-arm the watcher after every wake (the text says it no longer does).
tradeoff: Supervision survives a forgetful or interrupted model, but each harness needs its own re-arm owner and the text claims no zero-latency guarantee.
reversal_cost: High (inferred): five harness adapters and the turn-end guard each carry part of the contract.

decision: A secondmate is relaunched automatically only when its endpoint is proven dead or missing.
alternatives: Relaunch on an ambiguous, unreadable or unverified reading too.
tradeoff: No duplicate endpoint is created beside a live one, but a mate whose state cannot be read is left untouched and nothing here recovers it.
reversal_cost: Low (inferred): one classification test in the shared liveness library.

decision: Automatic secondmate relaunch is capped at 3 attempts per mate in 3600 seconds, after which it parks and escalates once.
tradeoff: A crash-looping mate cannot burn endless relaunches, but a mate that fails a fourth time in an hour waits for the agent or captain.
reversal_cost: Low (inferred): the cap and window are two configuration values.

decision: After a successful update, a live secondmate is restarted whether or not its tracked files changed.
alternatives: Restart only the homes whose instruction files changed in the git diff.
Only nudge the mate to re-read its instructions.
tradeoff: Launch-time wiring is always refreshed, but every update interrupts every live mate whose runtime can prove a restart.
reversal_cost: Moderate (inferred): the restart and nudge sets are computed together and reported as disjoint lists.

decision: Where a harness can deliver it, the session-start digest is delivered again after compaction.
alternatives: Re-run the start script by hand after each compaction.
tradeoff: A compacted session regains its recovery input without an agent step, but Codex's interactive UI and Cursor have no such channel and stay uncovered.
reversal_cost: Moderate (inferred): each covered harness needs its own adapter and tests.

decision: The captain's away words are recorded verbatim and read by the supervising agent's judgment, not parsed by any script.
alternatives: Parse the words into per-task grants, verbs or clauses that a script enforces.
tradeoff: The mandate stays as the captain wrote it, but only the mechanical limits (a merge green at its live head, synchronous merges, the spend cap) are enforced by code; the rest rests on the agent's reading.
reversal_cost: High (inferred): the record schema, read-back and branch prompt all assume no parser.
